# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition Records: Stations 17–345

## 1. Scope and Data Overview

This report analyzes 18 operating records spanning five asset classes — separators (3), scrubbers (6), heat exchangers (2), compressors (3), reactors (1), and pipelines (3) — across stations 17 through 345. Each record contains five measured parameters: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration (mm/s RMS), and efficiency (%).

Because the records are single snapshots rather than time series, this analysis is necessarily inferential. The approach is to (a) benchmark each reading against typical operating envelopes for the asset class, (b) identify internal inconsistencies within each record (parameters that don't co-vary as physics would suggest), and (c) prioritize follow-up measurements and maintenance actions. Where a single reading is ambiguous, I flag it as such rather than over-claiming a diagnosis.

**Preliminary data quality note:** Record 0000017 (pipeline, station 293) reports a process temperature of **−9 °C**. Unless this line carries refrigerated product or is upstream of a Joule–Thomson expansion, this is either a sensor fault (open-circuit thermocouple reading ambient/range-minimum) or genuine hydrate-formation risk territory. It is treated as a high-priority anomaly below.

---

Before unit-by-unit analysis, several fleet-wide patterns deserve attention:

Each record contains five process/condition parameters: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration velocity (mm/s RMS), and thermal/operational efficiency (%).

Because the dataset is a single snapshot per unit, this analysis is necessarily inferential. The intent is to (a) identify units whose parameter combinations suggest active or incipient failure modes, (b) specify the additional measurements needed to confirm or rule out each hypothesis, and (c) define concrete, prioritized maintenance actions. This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning five asset classes — separators (6), condensers (4), scrubbers (3), turbines (2), compressors (1), and valves (1) — across 17 stations. # Technical Analysis of Plant Equipment Records — Stations 39–303

## 1. Scope and Data Overview

This report analyzes 18 operational records spanning six equipment classes — turbines, compressors, condensers, valves, scrubbers, and separators — across 17 distinct stations. Each record contains five measured parameters: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration (mm/s RMS), and efficiency (%).

**Summary statistics across the dataset:**

| Parameter | Min | Max | Mean | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pressure | 107 kPa | 860 kPa | ~415 kPa | Wide spread; several units near atmospheric |
| Temperature | −3 °C | 169 °C | ~95 °C | Two units below 10 °C (possible cryogenic/chilled service) |
| Flow | 68 m³/h | 827 m³/h | ~440 m³/h | Two units below 120 m³/h (possible low-load or restriction) |
| Vibration | 0.1 mm/s | 8.2 mm/s | ~3.1 mm/s | Four units exceed 4.4 mm/s — the key risk cluster |
| Efficiency | 73% | 93% | ~83% | Four units at or below 79% |

The most actionable signal in this dataset is **vibration**. Per ISO 10816/20816 guidance for medium-sized rotating machinery, values above ~4.5 mm/s RMS indicate unsatisfactory operation warranting corrective action, and values above ~7 mm/s indicate the danger zone. Four units fall in or near these bands, and two of those are severe.

---

## 2. Unit-by-Unit Analysis

### 2.1 High-Priority Concerns

**Record 0000007 — Heat Exchanger 1644, Station 51 (8.2 mm/s, 82% eff.)**
This is the single worst vibration reading in the dataset and sits firmly in the ISO "danger" zone. For a heat exchanger, sustained vibration at this level typically indicates **flow-induced vibration (FIV)** on the tube side — vortex shedding or acoustic resonance causing tube bundle fretting. The risk is tube-to-tubesheet joint failure and tube rupture, which for a pressurized system (546 kPa, 105 °C) could mean a loss-of-containment event.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition Monitoring Records (Records 0000000–0000017)

## 1. Scope and Methodology

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning six asset classes (pumps, turbines, compressors, heat exchangers, condensers, separators, valves, and a reactor) across stations 10–387. Each record contains five measured parameters: discharge/line pressure (kPa), process temperature (°C), volumetric flow (m³/h), casing vibration velocity (mm/s RMS), and reported efficiency (%).

Because the dataset lacks nameplate data, baseline signatures, and trend history, this analysis proceeds by:

1. **Cross-asset benchmarking** — comparing each unit against the fleet-wide distribution for its parameter set.
2. **Physical plausibility screening** — flagging parameter combinations inconsistent with the asset type (e.g., a compressor with low discharge pressure, a valve with high vibration).
3. **Failure-mode inference** — mapping abnormal signatures to dominant failure modes per equipment class, using ISO 10816/20816 vibration severity zones and typical thermal-hydraulic expectations.
4. **Prioritized maintenance recommendations** — ranked by risk (probability × consequence).

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition-Monitoring Records (Records 0000000–0000017)

## 1. Scope and Method

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning six asset classes (turbine, scrubber, pipeline, pump, separator, condenser, reactor, valve) across 17 stations. Each record contains five measured parameters: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration (mm/s RMS), and efficiency (%). Because the dataset contains no explicit alarm limits, this analysis applies standard industry reference bands (ISO 10816/20816 vibration severity zones, typical thermal-efficiency expectations by equipment class, and process-envelope reasoning) to identify anomalies, infer likely failure modes, and prioritize maintenance actions.

**Reference bands used throughout:**

| Vibration (mm/s RMS) | ISO 10816 zone | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| < 0.7 | Zone A | New/commissioned equipment |
| 0.7 – 2.8 | Zone B | Unrestricted long-term operation |
| 2.8 – 7.1 | Zone C | Restricted operation; plan corrective action |
| > 7.1 | Zone D | Damage risk; action required |

Efficiency expectations by class (typical): turbines 85–95%, pumps 70–85%, condensers assessed by approach/heat-transfer effectiveness rather than shaft efficiency, scrubbers/valves/pipelines assessed against design duty.

---

## 2. Record-by-Record Assessment

### Record 0000000 — Turbine, Unit 6308, Station 112
**P 244 kPa | T 175 °C | Q 644 m³/h | Vib 3.4 mm/s | η 95%**

- **Vibration:** 3.4 mm/s falls in Zone C — acceptable only for restricted operation. For a turbine, this is an early bearing or balance warning.
- **Efficiency:** 95% is at the top of the expected band; no thermodynamic degradation is evident.
- **Pressure/temperature:** 244 kPa at 175 °C is a plausible steam/gas inlet condition; no red flag in isolation.
- **Likely failure modes:** incipient rotor imbalance (blade fouling or deposit loss), early-stage journal bearing wear, or misalignment developing after a thermal transient. The combination of *high efficiency + elevated vibration* is classic
